frente: A 68-year-old man has a resting tremor, bradykinesia and cogwheel rigidity. Loss of which neurons explains his motor findings?
verso: Dopaminergic neurons of the substantia nigra pars compacta
extra: Less dopamine reduces D1 excitation of the direct pathway and D2 inhibition of the indirect pathway. Both changes increase inhibitory output from the internal globus pallidus to the thalamus, so movement is harder to initiate. Surviving neurons contain α-synuclein Lewy bodies.
fonte: Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th ed.

frente: Carbidopa, which does not cross the blood-brain barrier, is combined with levodopa to inhibit peripheral {{c1::DOPA decarboxylase}}.
extra: Blocking conversion of levodopa to dopamine outside the CNS (the enzyme is also called aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase) leaves more levodopa to enter the brain and reduces peripheral dopamine effects such as nausea and orthostatic hypotension.
nota_pt: No Brasil a levodopa também é associada à benserazida, que tem o mesmo mecanismo da carbidopa.
fonte: Katzung Basic & Clinical Pharmacology, 15th ed.

frente: A 55-year-old man with long-standing alcohol use disorder has a wide-based gait and truncal ataxia, but finger-to-nose testing is normal. Degeneration of which structure is most likely?
extra: The vermis coordinates axial and proximal muscles used for stance and gait, while the cerebellar hemispheres coordinate the ipsilateral limbs. Alcohol-related degeneration preferentially affects the anterior superior vermis, so gait fails before limb coordination.
fonte: Adams and Victor's Principles of Neurology, 12th ed.

frente: After a right hemisection of the spinal cord at T10, on which side is pain and temperature sensation lost below the lesion?
verso: Left side, starting one to two segments below the lesion
extra: Spinothalamic fibers cross in the anterior white commissure within one or two segments of entry, so the lesion interrupts fibers from the opposite side. Dorsal column fibers ascend ipsilaterally and cross in the medulla, so vibration and proprioception are lost on the right.
fonte: Moore Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 9th ed.

frente: The amyloid precursor protein gene lies on chromosome {{c1::21}}, which explains early-onset Alzheimer disease in adults with Down syndrome.
extra: A third copy of APP increases production of amyloid-β peptide, which aggregates into extracellular plaques decades earlier than in the general population.
fonte: Thompson & Thompson Genetics in Medicine, 9th ed.

frente: Which antiseizure drug treats childhood absence epilepsy by blocking T-type calcium channels in thalamic neurons?
extra: T-type Ca<sup>2+</sup> currents generate the rhythmic burst firing of thalamocortical neurons that appears as 3-Hz spike-and-wave discharges on EEG. Reducing these currents interrupts the oscillation.
nota_pt: Etossuximida. O valproato também trata crises de ausência, mas age por vários mecanismos.
fonte: Katzung Basic & Clinical Pharmacology, 15th ed.

frente: A 19-year-old college student has fever, neck stiffness, a petechial rash and hypotension. CSF Gram stain shows gram-negative diplococci. Which bacterial component drives the shock and DIC?
extra: Neisseria meningitidis sheds outer membrane blebs rich in lipooligosaccharide, which triggers massive TNF-α and IL-1 release. Endothelial injury and activation of coagulation follow, and adrenal hemorrhage can occur (Waterhouse-Friderichsen syndrome).
fonte: Sherris & Ryan's Medical Microbiology, 8th ed.

frente: Thiazide diuretics can precipitate lithium toxicity because volume contraction increases lithium reabsorption in the {{c1::proximal tubule}}.
extra: The kidney handles lithium like sodium. Mild volume depletion increases proximal Na<sup>+</sup> reabsorption, and lithium is reabsorbed along with it. NSAIDs and ACE inhibitors raise lithium levels by reducing renal clearance.
fonte: Katzung Basic & Clinical Pharmacology, 15th ed.

frente: A 24-year-old man has had persecutory delusions and auditory hallucinations for 3 months, with no mood episodes, substance use or medical cause. What is the most likely diagnosis?
extra: DSM-5-TR separates primary psychotic disorders by duration: brief psychotic disorder lasts at least 1 day but less than 1 month, schizophreniform disorder 1 to 6 months, and schizophrenia at least 6 months including prodromal or residual phases.
fonte: Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, 5th ed., Text Revision (DSM-5-TR)

frente: A woman taking sertraline receives linezolid and develops hyperthermia, agitation, diarrhea and inducible ankle clonus. Which drug counteracts the underlying receptor overstimulation?
extra: Linezolid is a weak monoamine oxidase inhibitor, so serotonin accumulates when combined with an SSRI. Cyproheptadine antagonizes 5-HT<sub>2A</sub> receptors. Clonus and hyperreflexia distinguish serotonin syndrome from the lead-pipe rigidity of neuroleptic malignant syndrome.
fonte: Katzung Basic & Clinical Pharmacology, 15th ed.

frente: High-frequency sounds are detected at the {{c1::base}} of the cochlea, where the basilar membrane is narrow and stiff.
extra: Stiffness of the basilar membrane falls from base to apex, so each frequency produces maximal displacement at a different point (tonotopy). Hair cells at the base receive the most mechanical stress, which is why noise-induced and age-related hearing loss affect high frequencies first.
fonte: Kandel Principles of Neural Science, 6th ed.

frente: Why does oculomotor nerve compression by a posterior communicating artery aneurysm dilate the pupil early, while a diabetic oculomotor palsy usually spares it?
verso: Pupillary parasympathetic fibers run on the surface of the nerve
extra: External compression reaches the superficial parasympathetic fibers first, so mydriasis appears early. Diabetic microvascular ischemia damages the core of the nerve, producing ptosis and a down-and-out eye with a normal pupil.
fonte: Adams and Victor's Principles of Neurology, 12th ed.

frente: A 62-year-old has a mass crossing the corpus callosum. Histology shows necrosis bordered by pseudopalisading tumor cells and microvascular proliferation, and the tumor is IDH-wildtype. What is the diagnosis?
extra: Hypoxia around rapidly growing tumor drives cells to migrate away from necrotic centers (pseudopalisading) and induces VEGF-driven vessel proliferation. Under the 2021 WHO classification, glioblastoma is by definition IDH-wildtype; an IDH-mutant tumor with these features is an astrocytoma, IDH-mutant, grade 4.
fonte: WHO Classification of Tumours: Central Nervous System Tumours, 5th ed. (2021)

frente: Oligoclonal IgG bands present in CSF but absent from serum indicate {{c1::intrathecal}} antibody synthesis, supporting a diagnosis of multiple sclerosis.
extra: Clonally expanded B cells and plasma cells inside the CNS produce the immunoglobulin. CSF-specific bands appear in most patients with multiple sclerosis but are not specific to it, because CNS infections and other inflammatory diseases can also produce them.
fonte: Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th ed.

frente: A single {{c1::oligodendrocyte}} myelinates segments of many CNS axons, whereas each Schwann cell myelinates one internode of a single peripheral axon.
extra: Because one oligodendrocyte supports many axons, its loss in multiple sclerosis demyelinates several axons at once. Schwann cells also guide axon regrowth along their basal lamina, which helps explain why peripheral nerves regenerate better than central tracts.
fonte: Ross Histology: A Text and Atlas, 8th ed.

frente: A 7-year-old screams and appears terrified during the first hours of sleep, cannot be consoled and has no memory of it next morning. During which sleep stage do these episodes arise?
extra: Slow-wave sleep, with high-amplitude delta waves, is concentrated in the first third of the night. Night terrors and sleepwalking are partial arousals from N3, which explains the amnesia; nightmares arise from REM sleep, which predominates toward morning and is usually remembered.
fonte: Kaplan & Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 12th ed.

frente: Why must the azathioprine dose be sharply reduced when allopurinol is started?
verso: Allopurinol blocks xanthine oxidase, which inactivates 6-mercaptopurine
extra: Azathioprine is converted to 6-mercaptopurine. With xanthine oxidase inhibited, more 6-MP is shunted to active thioguanine nucleotides, which can cause severe myelosuppression.
fonte: Katzung Basic & Clinical Pharmacology, 15th ed.

frente: Calcium pyrophosphate crystals in pseudogout are rhomboid and show {{c1::weakly positive}} birefringence under polarized light.
extra: Positive birefringence makes the crystals look blue when parallel to the compensator axis. Monosodium urate crystals in gout are needle-shaped, strongly negatively birefringent and look yellow in the same orientation.
nota_pt: Doença por depósito de pirofosfato de cálcio (pseudogota).
fonte: Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th ed.

frente: A 28-year-old woman has ptosis and diplopia that worsen through the day. In most such patients, autoantibodies are directed against which target?
extra: Antibody binding causes receptor internalization and complement-mediated damage to the junctional folds (type II hypersensitivity). Fewer receptors lower the safety margin of transmission, so weakness grows with repeated use and repetitive stimulation shows a decremental response.
nota_pt: Miastenia gravis. Uma minoria dos pacientes tem anticorpos anti-MuSK.
fonte: Janeway's Immunobiology, 10th ed.

frente: In Lambert-Eaton syndrome, strength briefly improves with repeated contraction because {{c1::calcium}} accumulates in the presynaptic terminal.
extra: Autoantibodies against presynaptic P/Q-type voltage-gated Ca<sup>2+</sup> channels reduce acetylcholine release. Rapid repeated firing lets residual Ca<sup>2+</sup> build up, so release and strength transiently rise. Most paraneoplastic cases occur with small cell lung carcinoma.
fonte: Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th ed.

frente: Duchenne muscular dystrophy usually results from {{c1::frameshift}} deletions in the dystrophin gene, while in-frame deletions cause the milder Becker form.
extra: A frameshift creates a premature stop codon, so almost no dystrophin is made and the sarcolemma tears during contraction. An in-frame deletion yields a shorter but partly functional protein.
fonte: Thompson & Thompson Genetics in Medicine, 9th ed.

frente: A 3-year-old has had several fractures after minor falls and has blue sclerae. A defect in which protein is most likely?
extra: Most cases of osteogenesis imperfecta are autosomal dominant mutations in COL1A1 or COL1A2. Null alleles reduce the amount of normal collagen and cause the mild form, while glycine substitutions in the Gly-X-Y repeat disrupt triple-helix folding and cause the severe forms. The thin collagenous sclera lets the underlying choroid show through.
nota_pt: Osteogênese imperfeita. Na prova, considere sempre o diagnóstico diferencial com maus-tratos.
fonte: Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry, 8th ed.

frente: After a fracture of the surgical neck of the humerus, a patient cannot abduct the arm beyond 15 degrees and has numbness over the lateral shoulder. Which nerve is injured?
extra: The axillary nerve wraps around the surgical neck with the posterior circumflex humeral artery. It supplies the deltoid, which abducts the arm after the supraspinatus starts the movement, and the skin over the lower deltoid.
fonte: Moore Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 9th ed.

frente: A midshaft humeral fracture can injure the {{c1::radial}} nerve in the spiral groove, causing wrist drop.
extra: The radial nerve supplies the extensors of the wrist and fingers. Branches to the triceps usually leave above the groove, so elbow extension is often preserved.
fonte: Moore Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 9th ed.

frente: In a cutaneous melanoma without distant spread, which histologic measurement is the strongest predictor of nodal metastasis?
verso: Breslow thickness (depth of invasion in millimeters)
extra: Once melanoma enters its vertical growth phase, deeper invasion brings tumor cells close to dermal lymphatics and vessels. The AJCC 8th edition defines the T category by Breslow thickness and ulceration.
fonte: AJCC Cancer Staging Manual, 8th ed.

frente: Bullous pemphigoid causes tense subepidermal blisters because IgG targets {{c1::hemidesmosome}} proteins BP180 and BP230.
extra: Antibody and complement deposit along the basement membrane and recruit eosinophils, which split the epidermis from the dermis. The blister roof is the full epidermis, so blisters stay tense and the Nikolsky sign is negative, unlike the intraepidermal acantholysis of pemphigus vulgaris.
fonte: Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th ed.

frente: A gardener develops an ulcerated nodule on the hand, followed by new nodules along the lymphatics of the forearm. Which organism is most likely?
extra: Sporothrix is a dimorphic fungus that lives as a mold in soil and plant matter and converts to cigar-shaped yeast at body temperature after traumatic inoculation. It spreads along lymphatic channels and is treated with itraconazole.
nota_pt: No Brasil predomina a esporotricose zoonótica, transmitida por gatos e causada sobretudo por Sporothrix brasiliensis.
fonte: Sherris & Ryan's Medical Microbiology, 8th ed.

frente: Which supplement is prescribed routinely with weekly low-dose methotrexate for rheumatoid arthritis to reduce its adverse effects?
extra: Methotrexate inhibits dihydrofolate reductase, depleting the tetrahydrofolate needed for purine and thymidine synthesis in rapidly dividing cells such as mucosa and marrow. Folic acid supplementation lowers gastrointestinal and hepatic adverse effects without clear loss of efficacy; leucovorin (folinic acid), which bypasses the blocked enzyme, is the rescue drug for overdose or severe toxicity.
fonte: Shea B et al. Folic acid and folinic acid for reducing side effects in patients receiving methotrexate for rheumatoid arthritis. Cochrane Database Syst Rev. 2013;(5):CD000951.

frente: A child with osteopetrosis has very dense bones on radiographs yet develops pancytopenia and hepatosplenomegaly. What causes the cytopenias?
verso: Unresorbed bone fills the marrow cavity
extra: Osteoclasts cannot acidify the resorption pit (for example, carbonic anhydrase II or CLCN7 defects), so bone is laid down without remodeling. Medullary space is lost and hematopoiesis moves to the liver and spleen.
fonte: Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th ed.

frente: A 46,XY infant has ambiguous external genitalia but normal epididymis, vas deferens and seminal vesicles, and virilizes at puberty. Which enzyme is deficient?
extra: Wolffian ducts respond to testosterone, but the external genitalia and prostate need dihydrotestosterone. At puberty, high testosterone levels and the type 1 isoenzyme provide enough androgen action to virilize.
fonte: Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 15th ed.

frente: A man with type 2 diabetes starts a new oral drug and develops glucosuria with near-normal blood glucose and a genital fungal infection. Which transporter does the drug inhibit?
verso: SGLT2 in the proximal convoluted tubule
extra: SGLT2 reabsorbs most filtered glucose. Blocking it lowers the renal threshold, so glucose is lost in urine even at modest plasma levels. The lower insulin-to-glucagon ratio also favors ketogenesis, which explains euglycemic ketoacidosis.
fonte: Katzung Basic & Clinical Pharmacology, 15th ed.

frente: Metformin lowers fasting glucose mainly by reducing hepatic {{c1::gluconeogenesis}}, so used alone it rarely causes hypoglycemia.
extra: Metformin decreases hepatic glucose output, partly by inhibiting mitochondrial respiration and activating AMP-activated protein kinase; the exact mechanism is still debated. It does not stimulate insulin release, so hypoglycemia is uncommon. It is cleared by the kidney, and accumulation in severe renal impairment can cause lactic acidosis.
fonte: Katzung Basic & Clinical Pharmacology, 15th ed.

frente: Why does primary adrenal insufficiency cause skin hyperpigmentation, while secondary adrenal insufficiency does not?
verso: Excess ACTH stimulates melanocortin-1 receptors on melanocytes
extra: Low cortisol removes negative feedback, so pituitary corticotrophs increase POMC synthesis and ACTH secretion. ACTH contains the α-MSH sequence and binds MC1R, raising melanin synthesis. In pituitary disease ACTH is low, so the skin is not darkened.
fonte: Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 15th ed.

frente: Long-standing Hashimoto thyroiditis increases the risk of primary thyroid {{c1::B-cell lymphoma}}.
extra: Chronic autoimmune stimulation creates lymphoid follicles with germinal centers inside the thyroid, where B-cell clones can expand and transform. A rapidly enlarging goiter in such a patient raises this suspicion.
fonte: Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th ed.

frente: A woman treated for Graves disease with total thyroidectomy years ago delivers a tachycardic newborn with goiter. What explains the newborn's hyperthyroidism?
verso: Maternal TSH receptor-stimulating IgG crossed the placenta
extra: Thyroidectomy removes the target gland but not the autoantibody-producing B cells, so the mother may remain euthyroid on levothyroxine with high antibody titers. IgG crosses the placenta and stimulates the fetal thyroid until it is cleared over weeks to months after birth.
fonte: Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 15th ed.

frente: A thyroid nodule biopsy shows cells with optically clear nuclei, nuclear grooves and intranuclear pseudoinclusions. What is the diagnosis?
extra: The diagnosis rests on nuclear features rather than architecture. These tumors often carry BRAF V600E or RET fusions, are linked to childhood radiation exposure and spread mainly through lymphatics to cervical nodes.
fonte: Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th ed.

frente: Medullary thyroid carcinoma in MEN2A and MEN2B arises from germline gain-of-function mutations in the {{c1::RET}} proto-oncogene.
extra: RET encodes a receptor tyrosine kinase; constitutive activation drives proliferation of calcitonin-secreting parafollicular C cells. Carriers are offered prophylactic thyroidectomy, timed by the specific mutation.
fonte: Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 15th ed.

frente: A 30-year-old woman with a prolactinoma has amenorrhea, galactorrhea and low LH and FSH. How does excess prolactin cause the amenorrhea?
verso: It suppresses pulsatile GnRH release from the hypothalamus
extra: Fewer GnRH pulses lower LH and FSH, so follicles do not mature and estradiol falls (hypogonadotropic hypogonadism). Hypothalamic dopamine normally inhibits lactotrophs, which is why dopamine agonists such as cabergoline lower prolactin and usually restore ovulation.
fonte: Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 15th ed.

frente: Why is propylthiouracil preferred over methimazole for hyperthyroidism during the first trimester of pregnancy?
extra: First-trimester methimazole exposure is linked to aplasia cutis and a methimazole embryopathy that includes choanal and esophageal atresia. Propylthiouracil carries a risk of severe hepatotoxicity, so its use is limited to early pregnancy; the 2017 ATA guideline considers it unclear whether patients should switch to methimazole after the first trimester.
fonte: 2017 Guidelines of the American Thyroid Association for the Diagnosis and Management of Thyroid Disease During Pregnancy and the Postpartum

frente: A bodybuilder injecting testosterone has a low sperm count and small testes. What is the mechanism?
extra: Exogenous androgen inhibits GnRH, LH and FSH. Without LH, Leydig cells stop producing the high local testosterone that spermatogenesis needs, and without FSH, Sertoli cell support falls, even though serum testosterone is high.
fonte: Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th ed.

frente: The mid-cycle LH surge occurs when sustained high estradiol switches its effect on the pituitary from negative to {{c1::positive}} feedback.
extra: The dominant follicle secretes rising estradiol. Once levels stay high long enough, gonadotropes become more responsive to GnRH and release a large LH pulse that triggers ovulation.
fonte: Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th ed.

frente: A 32-year-old woman with polycystic ovary syndrome has had oligomenorrhea for years. Why is her risk of endometrial carcinoma increased?
verso: Chronic estrogen exposure unopposed by progesterone
extra: Without ovulation there is no corpus luteum, so progesterone never opposes estrogen-driven endometrial proliferation. Persistent proliferation leads to hyperplasia, the precursor of endometrioid carcinoma.
fonte: Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th ed.

frente: A man has purulent urethral discharge, and Gram stain shows intracellular gram-negative diplococci. Antigenic variation of which surface structure explains why reinfection is common?
extra: Neisseria gonorrhoeae recombines silent pilin gene copies into the expressed pilin locus, constantly changing the pilus antigen. Antibodies from a prior infection no longer recognize the new pili, so infection does not leave lasting protective immunity.
fonte: Sherris & Ryan's Medical Microbiology, 8th ed.

frente: High-risk HPV promotes cervical carcinoma because the E6 protein targets {{c1::p53}} for degradation and E7 inactivates {{c2::Rb}}.
extra: Loss of p53 removes apoptosis and cell-cycle arrest after DNA damage, and loss of Rb releases E2F to drive S-phase entry. Integration of viral DNA into the host genome increases E6 and E7 expression.
fonte: Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th ed.

frente: A 16-year-old phenotypic female has primary amenorrhea, normal breast development, scant pubic hair, a blind vaginal pouch and no uterus. Karyotype is 46,XY. Which protein is defective?
extra: The testes secrete anti-Müllerian hormone, so no uterus forms. Testosterone is made but cannot act, so male external genitalia and sexual hair do not develop, while its aromatization to estradiol produces breasts.
nota_pt: Síndrome de insensibilidade completa aos androgênios.
fonte: Thompson & Thompson Genetics in Medicine, 9th ed.

frente: During hysterectomy, which structure is most at risk when the uterine artery is clamped near the lateral cervix?
extra: In the base of the broad ligament, the ureter passes just below the uterine artery close to the lateral cervix. A clamp placed too low or too lateral can crush or ligate it.
fonte: Moore Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 9th ed.

frente: Tight junctions between adjacent {{c1::Sertoli}} cells form the blood-testis barrier, which shields developing germ cells from the immune system.
extra: Spermatocytes and spermatids appear after immune tolerance is established, so their new antigens are seen as foreign. The barrier separates the basal compartment from the adluminal compartment where meiosis proceeds.
fonte: Ross Histology: A Text and Atlas, 8th ed.

frente: Neural tube defects result from failed closure of the neural tube during the {{c1::fourth}} week after fertilization.
extra: The cranial neuropore closes around day 25 and the caudal neuropore around day 28, often before pregnancy is recognized. This is why folic acid must be taken before conception; open defects leak alpha-fetoprotein into amniotic fluid and maternal serum.
fonte: Langman's Medical Embryology, 15th ed.

frente: According to the 2022 CDC and AAP milestone checklists, an infant who sits without support, passes a toy from one hand to the other and is wary of strangers has reached the milestones of which age?
extra: The 2022 CDC and AAP checklists place each milestone at the age by which 75% or more of children have reached it. Stranger anxiety reflects the emerging ability to tell familiar from unfamiliar faces.
nota_pt: Outros livros e a Caderneta da Criança do Ministério da Saúde usam critérios diferentes, por isso a idade de um mesmo marco pode variar entre referências. A referência usada aqui é a revisão americana de 2022.
fonte: Zubler JM et al. Evidence-informed milestones for developmental surveillance tools. Pediatrics. 2022;149(3):e2021052138.

frente: Why does ACE inhibitor exposure in the second and third trimesters cause oligohydramnios?
verso: Fetal glomerular filtration depends on angiotensin II
extra: Angiotensin II constricts the efferent arteriole and keeps fetal GFR up when perfusion pressure is low. Blocking it reduces fetal urine output, the main source of amniotic fluid in later pregnancy, and can cause renal tubular dysgenesis, limb contractures and pulmonary hypoplasia.
fonte: Katzung Basic & Clinical Pharmacology, 15th ed.
